deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This is a sheet from the reduction of Gauss's Hanoverian triangulation of 1821-1823. It lists the stations Göttingen Sternwarte, Meridianzeichen, Hohehagen, Hils, Brocken and Lichtenberg. Deister, Garssen, Falkenberg and others continue on the next page. It is a clean, finished table, not a derivation.

AZIMUTH CONVENTION. Azimuths are counted from SOUTH through WEST: 90° = W, 180° = N, 270° = E. Geographic checks support this:
- Hercules (Kassel) lies at about 56° from Hohehagen, i.e. SW.
- Brocken lies at 281° from Hils, i.e. ESE.
- Sternwarte lies at 244° from Hohehagen, i.e. ENE.
- Wurmberg lies at 357° from Brocken, i.e. nearly due S.

COLUMNS. For each station P and target Q the columns are as follows.
- (1) A0, the observed station azimuth in degrees, minutes and seconds.
- (2) c, a reduction for eccentricity (reductio ad centrum or eccentric target). Examples: -18.389" for Hohehagen to the meridian mark, -3.516" for Hohehagen to Sternwarte, +0.199/-0.205 at the mark.
- (3) d, the reduction of the direction from the ellipsoid to Gauss's conformal plane (the 'arc-to-chord' correction).
- (4) A1 = A0 + c + d, the plane azimuth.
- (5) D = A1(Q->P) - [A1(P->Q) ± 180°], the reciprocal discrepancy. On the Lichtenberg block a second, common correction e is added.
- (6) The half, (D+e)/2 (respectively (-D+e)/2 at the other end).
- (7) A2 = A1 + half, the final adjusted plane azimuth.

In column (7), A2(P->Q) and A2(Q->P) differ by exactly 180°. This is the plane condition that a straight line in the conformal map has reciprocal bearings differing by 180°.

WORKED EXAMPLE, Sternwarte-Hohehagen.
- 64°1'17.797" - 0.064 = 17.733".
- 244°1'20.676" - 3.516 + 0.127 = 17.287".
- D = 17.287 - 17.733 = -0.446". Half = 0.223".
- Both ends become 17.510" (64°1'17.510" and 244°1'17.510").

OTHER RECIPROCAL PAIRS, all reproduced exactly:
- Meridian mark-Hohehagen: 41.606/42.150 -> 41.878.
- Meridian mark-Sternwarte: 5.694/5.248 -> 5.471.
- Meridian mark-Hils: 11.250/11.153 -> 11.2015.
- Hohehagen-Hils: 17.548/18.215 -> 17.8815.
- Hohehagen-Brocken: 26.436/25.841 -> 26.1385.
- Hils-Lichtenberg: 29.394/29.258 -> 29.326.
- Hils-Brocken: 52.723/53.287 -> 53.005.
- Hils-Deister: 53.589/53.730 (next page) -> 53.6595.
- Brocken-Lichtenberg: 48.561/48.554 -> 48.5575.

LICHTENBERG BLOCK, with the extra common term e:
- Deister: e = +0.037. Lichtenberg side 48.312 + (0.330 + 0.037)/2 = 48.4955. Deister side 48.642 + (-0.330 + 0.037)/2 = 48.4955.
- Falkenberg: e = -0.329, final 1.6385.
- Garssen: e = +0.210, final 4.910.

These common terms (my inference) come from a further network condition. Most likely it is the side (sine) condition of the complete quadrilateral Lichtenberg-Deister-Garssen-Falkenberg, since angle closure is automatic once plane azimuths are single-valued.

PROJECTION ORIGIN (my inference). The reduction column fits Gauss's conformal (transverse-Mercator-type) plane with origin at the Göttingen observatory. To first order the arc-to-chord correction is d12 ≈ ρ·(x2 - x1)(2y1 + y2)/(6R²), with y the ordinate. Then:
- Lines whose two ends lie on the meridian through the observatory (Sternwarte to meridian mark, both directions) have d = 0, as in the table.
- For a line from the origin meridian (y1 = 0) to a point with ordinate y, the theory predicts d12/d21 = y/(-2y) = -1/2. The table gives -0.064/+0.127 (Sternwarte-Hohehagen) and -0.116/+0.233 (mark-Hohehagen).
- A rough magnitude check for Hohehagen-Hils (about 47-50 km) gives about 1-2", matching ±1.1-1.3".

MARGIN NUMBER. The figure 4.6744372 beside Hohehagen-Hils is very probably log10 of that side length. In metres this would be about 47,240 m (unit unsure).

UNRESOLVED ITEMS. Some rows carry half-corrections whose partner station is off this page:
- Sternwarte-Meisner: -0.982.
- Brocken-Meisner: +0.857.
- Brocken-Inselsberg: -0.0125.
Several rows are unreduced, i.e. one-way directions with no reciprocal.
errors: No arithmetic errors found: every A0+c+d=A1, every discrepancy D, every half and every final value checked is correct to 0.001".
Brocken->Hercules final entry is left incomplete ('57. 34').

Sternwarte->Nördl. M.Z.: the eccentricity entry +5.471" is numerically identical to the final adjusted azimuth offset of the mark (180°0'5.471"). This may be a coincidence, or the entry may have been filled in after the adjustment; its origin is unexplained on this page.
The half-corrections for Meisner (-0.982, +0.857) and Inselsberg (-0.0125) rely on reciprocal data not on this page, so they cannot be verified here.

results.what: Reduction of observed geodetic directions to a conformal plane via arc-to-chord corrections. The values are consistent with origin at the Göttingen observatory (zero correction on the origin meridian; ratio -1/2 for lines from the origin meridian).
results.modern_name: Gauss conformal (Gauss-Krüger / transverse Mercator) projection; direction (arc-to-chord, t-T) reduction
results.usually_credited_to: C. F. Gauss (Hanover survey, 1820s); published by Schreiber (1866) and Krüger (1912)

results.what: Provisional adjustment of reciprocal plane azimuths by splitting the discrepancy equally, so that forward and back azimuths differ by exactly 180°.
results.modern_name: Reciprocal azimuth (direction) mean; station/line adjustment in a plane coordinate system
results.usually_credited_to: standard geodetic practice; Gauss in the Hanover triangulation

results.what: Additional common corrections in the Lichtenberg-Deister-Garssen-Falkenberg net, apparently from a further network (side) condition.
results.modern_name: Condition-equation least-squares adjustment of a triangulation net (side/sine condition)

results.what: Reduction to centre for eccentric station/target positions (e.g. -18.389", -3.516").

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working table from Gauss's well-documented Hanoverian triangulation. It applies his conformal projection and reciprocal-azimuth adjustment, both known to be his and largely published in his Werke IX. The data are a valuable record, but there is no new mathematics here.

checkable.asserts: Hohehagen->Sternwarte: 1'20.676" - 3.516 + 0.127 = 1'17.287", written in seconds after the minute carry
Mean of reciprocal plane azimuths Sternwarte-Hohehagen gives 17.510"
Lichtenberg-Deister: both ends give the same final value 48.4955 with the common term +0.037
Ratio of arc-to-chord corrections Sternwarte->Hohehagen vs Hohehagen->Sternwarte is about -1/2, as predicted by d12 ∝ dx*(2*y1+y2) with y_Sternwarte = 0
Same -1/2 ratio for mark->Hohehagen vs Hohehagen->mark (mark on the origin meridian)
Margin log 4.6744372 corresponds to a distance of about 47,240 units (Hohehagen-Hils side)

transcription_corrections: Brocken block: 'Warmberg 1821/1823' should be 'Wurmberg' (Harz summit just S of Brocken, consistent with azimuth ≈357°).
Brocken block: 'Katlenrode[?]' is more likely 'Hüttenrode' (E of Brocken, consistent with azimuth ≈279°); only '...ttenrode' is legible.
Hohehagen block: 'Lüneburg[?]' is geographically impossible at azimuth 337° (SSE). The legible ending is '...ineburg', so the name is uncertain.

Hohehagen block: the target labelled 'Südl. M.Z.' is the same mark as the 'Meridianzeichen' station (azimuths 228°19'41.878" / 48°19'41.878"). That mark is seen from the Sternwarte at about 180° (north in Gauss's south-based azimuths), so 'Südl.' is doubtful; only '..dl. M.Z.' is clearly legible.
Hils block: 'Siedlingerberg[?]' — only '...lingerberg' is legible; the identification is uncertain.
Values written like '0,333,5' or '17.881,5' mean 0.3335 and 17.8815 (a half of the discrepancy, carried to four decimals).
